label: Psychic Hotline
release_notes: Fifth album from Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn; first in four years and first on their own label.
Built over four years at their Betty's studio in Chapel Hill, N.C., with more collaborators than before.
Adds distorted guitars, breakbeats, trip-hop and found sound to their electronic pop.
Lead single Concrete Glen; also Hot Slob and Flood Season. NACC #7 the week of Oct. 1. Four tracks carry FCC words, including On & On (shit x4).
Label not in the Zookeeper label table.
Written over about four years. Bandcamp says six different drummers play on it (via WUNC).
draft_comment: Electro-pop that wanders off into fuzz guitars, breakbeats and trip-hop, and comes back grinning. Too many FCCs, but the clean ones are worth it.

tracks.title: Entertainment & Coca-Cola
tracks.notes: Opens with a high-pitched wail that gives way to a soft melody (Plus One).

tracks.title: Flood Season
tracks.notes: Single with video. Reviewers read it as about a new climate normal or ongoing struggle (Song Bar, Treble).

tracks.title: Hot Slob
tracks.notes: Single with video; described as a punked-up summer anthem. Released June 10, 2026 (Shore Fire Media). Stereogum calls the guitar-heavy sound a surprising new direction. Song Bar hears 1990s alt rock, glam guitar and electro-pop. Drums by TJ Maiani, guitar by Jenn Wasner of Wye Oak (verify at Shore Fire or FLOOD).

tracks.title: Concrete Glen
tracks.notes: Lead single (July 21, 2026) with video by Aaron Anderson and Eric Timothy Carlson; samples Sigur Ros' "Svefn-g-englar" (Agaetis Byrjun, 1999) (mxdwn). Consequence calls it hazy electronic pop inspired by a surreal night out.

tracks.title: Back Again
tracks.notes: Video game synth riffs and big percussion pads (Treble). Wonky clarinet bridge (Spectrum Culture).

tracks.title: Sledge
tracks.notes: Distorted guitar and a repeated chant refrain (Treble).

tracks.title: Right to Left
tracks.notes: Spectrum Culture hears peace found in one's own collapse.

tracks.title: Jessica
tracks.notes: About the duo's friend Jessica, who died of sudden liver failure in 2023 (Paste).

tracks.title: On & On
tracks.notes: Grew from a seedling in the band's session files (Shore Fire press).
